title: Finite projective cohomology over an arbitrary affine Noetherian base
statement: For affine T with Noetherian Gamma(T,O), finite coordinate type N, a closed embedding j:Y -> P(N;T) [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], and quasi-coherent finitely presented module F [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], every H^q(Y,F) [pqf-def-cohomology] is finite over Gamma(T,O), with scalars restricted along (j followed by the projective projection).

proof.text: Identify affine T with Spec Gamma(T,O), transport the embedding, and use closed pushforward to reduce to coherent projective-space cohomology. These comparisons must commute with the base-ring action. Empty coordinates force Y empty.

Reindex nonempty finite coordinates by a standard finite coordinate type. The standard affine cover gives an upper degree bound. Descending induction using finite sums of twists and their coherent kernels proves projective-space cohomology finite, without proper coherence. Transport back linearly to the stated action.

proof_origin.note: M1 extracted an independent step of the specified Chow-twist argument; no use of general proper coherence.

theorem finite_H_projective_affine_independent
    {Y T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] [IsNoetherianRing Γ(T, ⊤)]
    (N : Type u) [Finite N] (j : Y ⟶ ℙ(N; T)) [IsClosedImmersion j]
    (F : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFinitePresentation] (q : ℕ) :
    letI : Module Γ(T, ⊤) (F.H q) :=
      Module.compHom _ (j ≫ (ℙ(N; T) ↘ T)).appTop.hom
    Module.Finite Γ(T, ⊤) (F.H q)
